definitions.explanation: Made at home or in-house, rather than purchased from a store or manufacturer. Commonly used for food, drinks, and crafts. In restaurant contexts, it means made on the premises.

examples.japanese: {自家製|じかせい}のパンを{焼|や}いた。
このレストランは{自家製|じかせい}パスタが{自慢|じまん}だ。
examples.english: This restaurant takes pride in its house-made pasta.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}が{毎年|まいとし}{自家製|じかせい}の{梅干|うめぼ}しを{漬|つ}けてくれる。
examples.english: My grandmother makes homemade pickled plums for us every year.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a noun modifier with の: {自家製|じかせい}の + noun. Very common on restaurant menus and product labels. Conveys a sense of quality and care compared to mass-produced alternatives.

Compared to {手作|てづく}り (handmade), {自家製|じかせい} emphasizes that something was made in-house or at home (the location), while {手作|てづく}り emphasizes that it was crafted by hand (the method).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自家製|じかせい}パン: homemade bread
- {自家製|じかせい}ソース: house-made sauce
- {自家製|じかせい}の{味噌|みそ}: homemade miso
- {自家製|じかせい}{麺|めん}: house-made noodles
